chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Aziz b. Yahya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Umarah from his father from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father Muhammad b. Ali from his truthful forefathers (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Surely, God, Blessed and Exalted, assigned to my brother Ali b. Abi Talib virtues which cannot be enumerated by anyone other than Him. So whoever mentions a virtue from his virtues, acknowledging it, God will forgive him his past sins and the latter ones, even if he were to come on the Day of Resurrection with the sins of the two heavyweights (men and jinn). Whoever writes down a virtue from the virtues of Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him), the angels shall not cease seeking forgiveness for him as long as a trace of that writing remains. Whoever listens to a virtue from his virtues, God will forgive him the sins which he acquired through hearing. Whoever looks at a writing about his virtues, God will forgive him the sins which he acquired through sight.

Then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Looking towards Ali b. Abi Talib is worship. His mention is worship. And the faith of a servant is not accepted except through his wilaya (authority/guardianship) and dissociation from his enemies.

key_terms.الثَّقَلَيْنِ: The two heavyweights — men and jinn, indicating the magnitude of sins that can be forgiven
key_terms.الْبَرَاءَةِ: Dissociation (bara'a) — the act of disavowing the enemies of Ali, paired with wilaya as a requirement of true belief
key_terms.عِبَادَةٌ: Worship — looking at Ali and mentioning him are equated with acts of devotion
key_terms.فَضَائِلَ: Virtues — innumerable excellences divinely assigned to Ali b. Abi Talib
key_terms.وِلَايَتِهِ: His wilaya (authority/guardianship) — the spiritual and political authority of Ali, acceptance of which is a condition of faith

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib and the reward for mentioning them?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition transmitted through the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet Muhammad (s) declares the innumerable virtues of his brother Ali b. Abi Talib. He explains that whoever mentions, writes, listens to, or reads about even one of Ali's virtues while acknowledging it will receive complete divine forgiveness. The Prophet concludes by asserting that looking at Ali is worship, mentioning him is worship, and no servant's faith is accepted without pledging allegiance to him (wilaya) and dissociating from his enemies. This hadith was delivered in the context of the Prophet establishing the spiritual and theological significance of Ali's station, echoing Quranic themes about the love of the Prophet's family.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abd al-`Aziz b. Yahya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us from [Ja`far b.] Muhammad b. `Imarah from his father from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father Muhammad b. `Ali from his truthful fathers (as).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Surely, Allah assigned virtues to my brother `Ali b. Abi Talib which cannot be enumerated by anyone other than Him. So, whoever mentions a virtue from his many virtues, acknowledging it, Allah will forgive him his past sins and the latter ones, even if he were to come on the Resurrection with the sins of the two heavyweights (men and jinn). Whoever writes down a virtue from the virtues of `Ali b. Abu Talib (as), the angels shall not descend but seeking forgiveness for him as long as that descriptive writing remains. Whoever listens to a virtue from his virtues, Allah will forgive him the sins which he would have acquired through his hearing. Whoever looks at a writing about his virtues, Allah will forgive him the sins which he would have acquired through sight.

Then the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Looking towards `Ali b. Abu Talib is worship. His mention is worship. And the faith of a servant is not accepted save through his wilaya and dissociation from his enemies.
